parsed.explanation: The combined regime pairs formal 1976 decriminalisation with operative police powers: morality/indecency articles (3–24 months, fines, deportation for non-citizens) documented as used against people suspected of LGBTQI+ identity or cross-dressing, including a 2009 cross-dressing conviction and a 2011 raid, plus further moral legislation in Feb 2024. Entry is a documented universal exposure: the Interior Minister stated suspected effeminate homosexuals are barred via airport checks, and pending bills would bar LGBTQ foreigners. No anti-discrimination or hate-speech protection exists; recourse is thin and research is blocked. No execution or custodial torture is documented, so this sits below the 0.15 tier but above the 0.35 administrative-restriction anchors because imprisonment is documented as actually applied.

entry_documents.exposure: Interior Minister stated suspected effeminate homosexuals are banned from entry via airport checks; pending bills propose barring LGBTQ foreigners; indecency provisions carry deportation for non-citizens. Presentation, not just documents, is the trigger.
entry_documents.protection: No documented formal requirement for marker disclosure; 1976 decriminalisation removes the sodomy charge at the border.
entry_documents.interaction: Border screening feeds into penal-code morality articles if secondary inspection escalates, moving a visitor from exclusion to prosecution and deportation.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Articles 324, 329, 350 supply arrest power used against suspected LGBTQI+ or cross-dressing people; 2009 one-month sentence for public cross-dressing; 2011 party raid; Article 330 mandates STI testing for those charged with prostitution or fujoor.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Sentences documented to date are short (one month); no documented custodial torture or execution for visitors.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A presentation-based entry stop can escalate into a morality charge, STI testing and deportation for a non-citizen.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No subnational variation documented; enforcement described only at state level. Article 330 permits relocation to a medical facility after a charge.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Country-wide application means no safer region can be identified from the record.

care_services.exposure: Courts refuse legal gender recognition and gender-affirming care citing Sharia (2023 rulings), limiting surgery to intersex cases; no LGBTQ organisations or shelters exist; registration of such groups improbable.
care_services.interaction: An outed visitor needing emergency or trans-related care faces institutionally hostile courts and no community fallback, though home-country prescriptions reduce exposure.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Officials frame LGBTQ people as entry threats; Feb 2024 moral legislation; hate speech unprotected (Art. 309 covers religious groups only); homosexuality used falsely to discredit critics; 2024 hostile caricature; education policy treats gender nonconformity as discipline.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: 1976 repeal and international readings hold same-sex intimacy formally legal.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official threat-framing legitimises police use of morality articles against presentation, and the unresolved sodomy-illegality conflict leaves outcome unpredictable.

minors_guardians.exposure: Pending bills would train teachers to spot homosexuality or cross-dressing for punishing children; a 2024 ministry investigation punished students for same-sex mock proposals. A gender-nonconforming minor travelling with a parent faces the same presentation-based entry screening.
minors_guardians.interaction: Youth are an explicit policy target, so a visible family group raises scrutiny and the stakes of any outing.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-specific violence rate or killing figure with a denominator is documented; police-initiated raids and morality-provision enforcement are documented instead. False homosexuality accusations are a known weapon.
street_violence_police_response.protection: No documented pattern of fatal anti-trans violence; sentences imposed have been brief.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Absence of violence data is uninformative given a decade of blocked human-rights research.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No discrimination or hate-crime protection; researchers denied entry for a decade; unresolved conflict over whether sodomy is illegal; pending bills' status unknown; Feb 2024 legislation contents undetailed.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts formally operate and the 1976 repeal is recognised by several international sources.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Thin, partly remote sourcing plus blocked oversight means an outed visitor has no reliable, documented remedy.

anchor_checks.comparison: Higher than this anchor: Karthovia's police checks end in release after hours with fines and 'detention rarely becomes imprisonment'. Here imprisonment under morality articles is documented as actually imposed on a cross-dressing person, plus deportation and a stated airport entry ban, so severity and state direction exceed 0.35-B.

Similar tier: Ostravia combines birth-sex custody, cross-dressing arrests in administrative buildings, brief sentences, no execution and slow remedies. This dossier matches that shape but adds a presentation-based national entry ban and 2024 moral legislation, so slightly lower than 0.25-C.

Higher than this anchor: Kestrel Isles secondary screening stays administrative — refusal and return — with written decisions and appeals. Here the border trigger feeds criminal morality provisions carrying imprisonment and deportation, and there is no documented effective remedy.

Far below this anchor: Meridia trains border staff, accepts congruent markers, guarantees counsel and compensation, and detention ends in brief release. This dossier documents the opposite institutional posture — official exclusion by presentation and no protections.

parsed.synthesis: Formal decriminalisation is outweighed by operative practice: morality and indecency articles are the live arrest power, documented against cross-dressing and suspected LGBTQI+ people, with imprisonment, fines and deportation available to a non-citizen. The border is the sharpest universal exposure — exclusion keyed to presentation, backed by an Interior Minister's statement and pending legislation — and any escalation there lands in the penal-code regime. No anti-discrimination, hate-speech or community infrastructure exists, researchers are blocked for a decade, and the unresolved sodomy-legality conflict adds unpredictability. No execution, torture or documented killing pattern is recorded, and sentences actually imposed have been short; thin sourcing limits confidence in both directions. For an adult alone or with a minor, discovery risks exclusion, short custody or deportation rather than catastrophe.
